root_idea.summary: The root centers on dust and the surface or color of the earth, with related extensions to force, ferocity, animal descriptions, and certain named plants, times, and objects.
root_idea.development: The lexical development proceeds from dust and dust-color to rubbing or casting into dust, then to strength and boldness; other Classical branches include a fire-producing tree, a monthly time expression, and animal terms.

senses.definition: A powerful, formidable being; in the Qurʾanic occurrence, a powerful jinn.
senses.usage_conditions: The Qurʾanic use applies the noun to a jinn. Strength and formidable physical constitution are central aspects of the description.

senses.definition: A cunning, wicked, rebellious, and audacious being; in the Qurʾanic occurrence, a jinn possessing these qualities.
senses.usage_conditions: The Qurʾanic use is specifically of a jinn. Classical Arabic also applies related forms to humans, but that human extension is not asserted as a separate Qurʾanic use here.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To rub or soil something with dust; to roll or turn it over in dust, hide it there, or be dust-defiled.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The participial adjective عافر describes something or someone covered or defiled with dust, especially the face.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cast someone to the ground, seize and throw him, wrestle with him, or make him cleave to the dust.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may describe dragging or throwing an adversary into the dust.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A dust-colored hue tending toward whitishness, often with a dull or reddish tinge; to be or become of that color.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The color is compared with the surface of the earth and may describe animals, land, or other objects.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of wild animals: to become fat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized Classical use of the Form V verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make white, or to become white.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The use is attested of mixed sheep or goats, food, and similar objects; it expresses whitening rather than dusting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become rubbed or soiled with dust, or to roll, turn over, or become hidden in dust.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the intransitive or medio-passive counterpart of dusting and rolling something in dust.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fail to reach the ground beneath one’s feet while entering water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the construction describing a person whose feet do not reach the bottom.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become or act like an عِفْرِيت: to behave with its formidable or mischievous character.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This specialized verb is derived from عِفْرِيت and preserves the augmentative ending of that noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A boar, swine, or young pig.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a distinct nominal use from the adjectival meanings of عِفْرٌ and عِفْرِيتٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A human who is wicked, crafty, audacious, rebellious, or exceptionally forceful; a person metaphorically likened to a devil.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the Classical human application of the same adjectival family whose Qurʾanic occurrence describes a jinn.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who or something that exceeds ordinary bounds, or is sharp, vigorous, and effective in an affair, especially with craft or malignity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression may describe unusual effectiveness or excess rather than physical strength alone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Strong, powerful, or bold, especially of a lion, lioness, or she-camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These adjectival forms are used of powerful animals and are distinct from the jinn designation عِفْرِيت.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dust, the outer layer of dust or earth, and the surface or face of the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The surface-of-the-earth sense also occurs in expressions meaning “upon the face of the earth.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression كَلَامٌ لَا عَفَرَ فِيهِ, speech containing nothing obscure or difficult to understand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a figurative idiom based on the absence of dust or obstruction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The hair or feathers at the back of the neck, crown, forelock, or around the neck of a bird.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may describe the raised hair or feathers of a person, lion, cock, bustard, or similar animal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In لَيْثُ عِفِرِّينَ, a lion; عِفِرِّين is also reported as the name of a place or country associated with lions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The phrase may function as a fixed designation or proverbially as an image of courage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small creeping creature said to resemble a chameleon, hide in soft dust, roll itself into a ball, and throw up dust when disturbed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a rare zoological designation and is separate from the place-name use in لَيْثُ عِفِرِّينَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fully mature and vigorous man, conventionally one who has reached fifty years of age.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a figurative age expression built on the image of the lion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Resolute, firm-minded, strong, or powerful.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This figurative adjectival use is reported independently of the zoological and place-name uses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A ghoul or similar demon.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This meaning is attributed to the feminine-form noun عَفَرْنَاةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tree whose wood produces abundant fire and is used for fire-drills or kindling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: عَفَارٌ may be a collective designation, with عَفَارَةٌ for an individual tree.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The quality or disposition of one who is wicked, malignant, or devilishly forceful.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This abstract noun denotes the characteristic associated with عِفْرٌ, عِفْرِيَةٌ, and عِفْرِيتٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression وَقَعُوا فِي عَافُورِ شَرٍّ, difficulty, distress, or a severe predicament.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression’s etymology is disputed: it may derive from this root or involve substitution for ث in عاثور.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A calamity, distress, or frightening predicament; in a related proverb, to carry a tyrant on the horn means to kill him and carry his head on a spear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression كَأَنَّهُ عَلَى قَرْنِ أَعْفَرَ describes someone frightened or disquieted. The proverb preserves an older image involving an antelope’s horn.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Red or reddish sand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a nominal use distinct from the general adjective for a whitish dust-color.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of land: untrodden or not yet traversed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective is applied specifically to land in the cited construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A designation for certain moonlit or pale nights, especially the thirteenth night or, in another usage, the seventh, eighth, and ninth nights of the lunar month.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Classical descriptions differ over which nights are included; the term is associated with the moon’s whiteness, while another expression contrasts white and dark nights.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One whose sheep or goats have the color called عُفْرَةٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is reported as a tribal or group designation in particular usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of land: land whose herbage has been eaten or grazed down.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized passive-participial description of land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who travels with groups of wayfarers and obtains a share of their surplus provisions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a figurative or specialized occupational description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A type of garment or cloth, including a garment of the kind called بُرْد.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name is related to Maʿāfir, understood as a Yemeni tribe, place, or district; the garment noun may occur without the relative suffix.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A dust-colored gazelle; by extension, a gazelle generally, a young gazelle, a buck-gazelle, or the young of a wild cow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The exact animal reference varies among Classical descriptions; the basic association is with a gazelle and its dust-colored appearance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A light or active ass.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a separate animal use from the gazelle designation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A human form seen from a distance and resembling a gazelle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a figurative visual comparison, not a name for a human being generally.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One of the traditional divisions of the night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is listed among five named divisions of the night.

cautions: The Qurʾanic occurrence of عِفْرِيت is a designation for a jinn; the human, animal, anatomical, color, and other extensions listed separately are broader Classical Arabic uses.
The Qurʾanic lexical profile combines formidable strength with craft, rebellion, or malignity; the contextual rendering “a strong one” does not exhaust the lexical evidence.
